tineBlockRef.language: Language used by this extension's messages, hovers, panels and tool results. Note: command titles and setting names follow the VS Code display language and cannot be overridden here.
tineBlockRef.language.enum.auto: Follow the VS Code display language (default)
tineBlockRef.graphRoot: Tine graph root directory. Leave empty to auto-detect a directory that contains both pages/ and logseq/.
tineBlockRef.include: File patterns to index, relative to the graph root.
tineBlockRef.exclude: Paths to exclude from indexing. Tine / Logseq metadata and recycle bins are excluded by default.
tineBlockRef.maxDepth: Default depth for expanding nested block references (a reference inside another referenced block). 0 disables recursion.
tineBlockRef.maxOutputChars: Output character budget for a single tool call. Content beyond it is truncated with a notice.
tineBlockRef.hoverPreviewLines: Number of block content lines shown in the hover preview. Fewer lines keep the popup short, so the Expand and Backlinks buttons at the bottom stay visible.
tineBlockRef.hideProperties: Property names to hide when rendering block content (without the trailing ::).
tineBlockRef.inlineRender.enabled: Show ((uuid)) inline as the target block's first line, similar to native Tine / Logseq rendering. When disabled, the raw UUID is shown.
tineBlockRef.inlineRender.mode: How block references are shown inline in the editor. `activeLine` shows the real ((uuid)) on the line your cursor is on and the target title everywhere else; it is the only mode where you can freely place the cursor, select, and edit references.
tineBlockRef.inlineRender.maxTitleLength: Maximum length of the target block title in inline rendering. Longer titles are truncated with an ellipsis so the line does not grow unbounded.
tineBlockRef.inlineRender.showMissing: Show "⚠ Block not found" inline instead of the raw UUID when the target block is missing, so broken references stand out immediately.
tineBlockRef.render.stripHeadingMarks: Strip Markdown heading marks (#, ##, ...) from block titles in inline rendering, hover preview and expanded documents. Content returned by AI tools keeps the marks so the model can still read the hierarchy.
tineBlockRef.showIndexNotification: Show a notification in the status bar area once the index has been built automatically. When disabled, a warning is still shown if the index is empty (no notes found).
tineBlockRef.backlinks.style: How backlink counts appear in the editor. Only blocks that are actually referenced show a marker, so most notes gain nothing.
tineBlockRef.backlinks.panel: How the backlinks panel is rendered. Links inside a text editor require Ctrl+Click (a VS Code rule); only the webview panel supports plain left-click.
tineBlockRef.backlinks.subtreeLines: Maximum subtree lines expanded per referencing block in the backlinks panel. 0 means unlimited (default), matching Tine. A few blocks in real vaults exceed 400 lines; set a value such as 30 to truncate them.
tineBlockRef.backlinks.itemsPerPage: Maximum references listed per page in the backlinks panel. The remainder is summarised so a heavily referenced block does not produce an endless panel.
tineBlockRef.backlinks.pathDepth: Number of ancestor levels shown as the breadcrumb for each referencing block. Deeper ancestors are dropped, keeping those closest to the reference.
tineBlockRef.inlineRender.mode.enum.acti: Show the target title, but reveal the real ((uuid)) on the line the cursor is on (recommended: fully editable)
tineBlockRef.inlineRender.mode.enum.repl: Always hide the raw UUID and show only the target block title (cleanest look, but the cursor can no longer reach the right side of a reference)
tineBlockRef.inlineRender.mode.enum.appe: Keep the raw UUID and append 〔target block title〕 after it (cursor behaves normally)
tineBlockRef.enterSplitBlock: In Tine / Logseq notes, pressing Enter inside a block splits it into two sibling blocks. Turn this off to get the plain VS Code newline behaviour.
tineBlockRef.backlinks.style.enum.inline: Show a "🔗 N" badge at the end of the block line; hover it to list pages that reference the block. Matches Tine (default)
tineBlockRef.backlinks.style.enum.lens: Show "N link references" on a separate line above the block. Use this when VS Code inlay hints are disabled (editor.inlayHints.enabled)
tineBlockRef.backlinks.style.enum.off: Show no backlink marker in the editor; the commands still work
tineBlockRef.backlinks.panel.enum.html: Webview panel: left-click a block title to jump, styled after Tine (default)
tineBlockRef.backlinks.panel.enum.text: Read-only text document: requires Ctrl+Click to jump, but supports Ctrl+F and free copying
tineBlockRef_readBlock.userDescription: Read a Tine / Logseq block and all of its children by UUID
tineBlockRef_readNote.displayName: Read Note and Expand Block References
tineBlockRef_readNote.userDescription: Read an entire Tine / Logseq note with all block references expanded
tineBlockRef_findBacklinks.userDescripti: Find which notes reference the given block UUID
tineBlockRef_readBlock.modelDescription:
Read the real content that a block reference (a UUID such as ((uuid))) points to in a Tine / Logseq note.

When you see ((66c73a56-ddda-44d2-80dd-009e44406fd4)) or {{embed ((66c73a56-...))}} in a .md note, you must call this tool to learn what it points to — the UUID itself carries no semantic information.

Returns: the target block's first line, all child blocks with their hierarchy preserved, the source file and line number, and the subtree size. If the target block does not exist the result says so explicitly (dangling reference). If the same UUID is defined in several places, all candidates are listed.

Use when: understanding what a "see ((uuid))" in a note means, expanding a block's entries, or tracing knowledge across files.
Not for: reading an entire note (use blockNote) or resolving [[page name]] links (not handled by this tool).
tineBlockRef_readBlock.blockIds.descript: UUIDs of the blocks to read, at most 20. A (( )) wrapper is accepted and stripped automatically.
tineBlockRef_readBlock.includeChildren.d: Whether to include child blocks. Defaults to true. Child blocks usually carry the actual content, so keep this enabled unless you only need the first line.
tineBlockRef_readBlock.compact.descripti: Compact mode: output only the first line of each block, useful for scanning many blocks quickly. Defaults to false.
tineBlockRef_readBlock.maxDepth.descript: Depth for expanding nested block references (a reference inside another referenced block). Defaults to the extension setting (3). 0 disables recursion.
tineBlockRef_readNote.modelDescription:
Read an entire Tine / Logseq note and expand every ((uuid)) block reference in it into its real content.

**When you need to read a .md note under pages/ or journals/, prefer this tool over the plain file-reading tool**: a plain read only shows a string of UUIDs, hides the referenced content, and will make you miss key context and draw one-sided conclusions.

mode parameter (important, directly affects output size):
- expand (default): expand the whole note. When there are more than 8 references a list is attached automatically; content beyond the output budget is not expanded and the unexpanded line numbers are listed at the end.
- list: **return only the reference list** (line number, UUID, target block first line), usually just a few KB. When there are many references (>10), or you only need to locate one, **prefer this mode** and then read specific blocks with blockRef.
- both: list plus expanded content.

Usage advice:
1. When unsure how many references a note has, start with mode=list.
2. Use mode=expand when you need the actual content.
3. If the result says some references were not expanded, read those UUIDs one by one with blockRef rather than falling back to plain file reading.

Content is generated in memory; no file is created or modified. If the file is open in the editor with unsaved changes, the current editor content is used.
tineBlockRef_readNote.filePath.descripti: Path to the note. Either an absolute path or a path relative to the graph root, for example pages/some-note.md.
tineBlockRef_readNote.includeChildren.de: Whether to include child blocks when expanding. Defaults to true.
tineBlockRef_readNote.maxDepth.descripti: Depth for expanding nested references. Defaults to the extension setting (3).
tineBlockRef_findBacklinks.modelDescript:
Find which notes reference the given block UUID (backlinks).

Use this to answer questions such as "where is this block referenced", "who cites this content", or "does this content appear elsewhere".

Returns, for each referencing location: file, line number, reference type (inline / embed), and the first line of the containing block. The definition location of the UUID is also given; duplicate definitions or a deleted target block are called out explicitly.
tineBlockRef_findBacklinks.blockId.descr: UUID of the target block. A (( )) wrapper is accepted.
tineBlockRef_findBacklinks.limit.descrip: Maximum number of references to return. Defaults to 50, maximum 200.
tineBlockRef_newId.userDescription: Generate fresh Tine / Logseq block IDs (UUID v4) with the exact id:: line and reference syntax
tineBlockRef_newId.modelDescription:
Generate one or more fresh persistent block IDs (UUID v4) for Tine / Logseq notes. Returns the exact `id::` property line, an inline reference `((uuid))`, an embed `{{embed ((uuid))}}`, and placement rules. Nothing is written to disk.

Use when: you are creating a new block that will be referenced elsewhere, or you need a UUID before writing `id::` and `((uuid))` yourself. Do not invent UUIDs; always use the values returned by this tool.

Important: put `id::` immediately after the block's first line, two spaces deeper than the block bullet, before body text and child blocks. If the block's first line is a code fence (for example `- ```js`), put `id::` after the closing fence and before child blocks; Logseq may not recognize it there.
tineBlockRef_newId.count.description: How many IDs to generate, 1-20. Defaults to 1.
tineBlockRef_newId.labels.description: Optional labels corresponding to each requested ID, so you can map UUIDs back to blocks without mixing them up.
tineBlockRef_findBlocks.displayName: Find Blocks by Title or Content
tineBlockRef_findBlocks.userDescription: Search Tine / Logseq blocks by title or body text and get their file, line, breadcrumb, and UUID
tineBlockRef_findBlocks.modelDescription:
Search Tine / Logseq blocks by title or body text. Returns candidates with file, 1-based line number, breadcrumb, UUID (or `needs id`), and subtree size. Results include unsaved editor content.

Use when: you need to find an existing block before referencing it. If a candidate has an ID, write `((uuid))` directly. If it has no ID, call `#blockMakeRef` with the candidate's file and line to get a patch. The search matches every whitespace-separated term; set `includeContent: true` to search block bodies, not just the first line.
tineBlockRef_findBlocks.query.descriptio: Block title or phrase. Multiple whitespace-separated terms must all match. Optional when filePath is given: leave it empty to list blocks in that note.
tineBlockRef_findBlocks.filePath.descrip: Optional: restrict the search to one note. Absolute path or path relative to the graph root.
tineBlockRef_findBlocks.limit.descriptio: Maximum number of candidates. Defaults to 10, maximum 200.
tineBlockRef_findBlocks.includeContent.d: Search block bodies (`ownLines`) instead of only the block first line. Defaults to false.
tineBlockRef_findBlocks.headingsOnly.des: Only return blocks whose first line is a Markdown heading (`# `, `## ` …). Combine with filePath and an empty query to list a note's outline in one call.
tineBlockRef_findBlocks.headingLevel.des: With headingsOnly: restrict to a single level (1 = `#`, 2 = `##` …).
tineBlockRef_makeRef.displayName: Prepare a Block Reference and Patch
tineBlockRef_makeRef.userDescription: Get the UUID, reference text, and a precise patch for adding id:: to a block that has none
tineBlockRef_makeRef.modelDescription:
Prepare everything needed to reference a specific block: the UUID, the reference text, and a precise `oldText` / `newText` patch (plus a unified diff fallback) for adding `id::` when the block has none.

Use when: `#blockFind` or a file read found the target block but it has no `id::`. Pass the file path, a 1-based line inside the block, and `expectedFirstLine` (the block's first line without `- `) so the tool can verify the target. Apply the returned patch with your own file editing tool, then write the reference, then call `#blockCheck`.

This tool never writes files. If the block already has an ID, it returns that ID and `existing: true`. If the target is invalid (page-leading implicit block, unclosed code fence, duplicate UUID), it explains why instead of guessing.
tineBlockRef_makeRef.filePath.descriptio: Path to the note. Absolute path or path relative to the graph root.
tineBlockRef_makeRef.line.description: 1-based line number inside the target block. The tool picks the deepest block containing that line.
tineBlockRef_makeRef.expectedFirstLine.d: The target block's first line without the leading `- ` (the raw first line is also accepted). Used to verify the target has not changed.
tineBlockRef_makeRef.kind.description: Reference form: `inline` for `((uuid))`, `embed` for `{{embed ((uuid))}}`. Defaults to inline.
tineBlockRef_link.userDescription: Resolve target blocks, add any missing id:: and write the references into a note in one step
tineBlockRef_link.modelDescription:
One-call replacement for the find → makeRef → write-reference chain. Resolves every target block, generates a UUID for any target that has no id::, and computes the exact reference blocks for the destination, returning all patches at once. Writes nothing: apply the patches with your file editing tool.

Use when: you need to reference one or more existing blocks from another note (or the same one). Typical flow: `#blockFind` (filePath + headingsOnly to see an outline, or a query to search) → this tool once → apply the patches → `#blockCheck` once. Do not re-read the files to verify the result.
tineBlockRef_link.filePath.description: Default note path for targets that do not set their own.
tineBlockRef_link.destination.descriptio: The block that should hold the references.
tineBlockRef_link.destination.filePath.d: Note path of the destination block. Absolute or relative to the graph root.
tineBlockRef_link.destination.line.descr: 1-based line number inside the destination block.
tineBlockRef_link.destination.expectedFi: Destination block first line, used to verify it has not moved.
tineBlockRef_link.destination.position.d: Append the references as child blocks (default) or as sibling blocks of the destination.
tineBlockRef_link.targets.description: Blocks to reference. Each one becomes a reference block.
tineBlockRef_link.targets.filePath.descr: Note path of this target; falls back to the top-level filePath.
tineBlockRef_link.targets.line.descripti: 1-based line number inside the target block.
tineBlockRef_link.targets.expectedFirstL: Target block first line, used to verify it has not moved.
tineBlockRef_link.targets.label.descript: Optional text placed before the reference, for example "Related".
tineBlockRef_checkRefs.userDescription: Audit a note for dangling references, duplicate UUIDs, misplaced id:: lines, and malformed references
tineBlockRef_checkRefs.modelDescription:
Audit a Tine / Logseq note for block ID and reference problems. Reports errors (dangling references, duplicate UUIDs, `id::` after body text, malformed `((...))`) and warnings (v8 runtime-style UUIDs, zero-indent IDs, IDs after a code fence). Nothing is written to disk.

Use when: after writing `id::` or `((uuid))` with your own editing tools, to verify the result before telling the user the note is done.
tineBlockRef_checkRefs.filePath.descript: Path to the note. Absolute path or path relative to the graph root.
tineBlockRef_checkRefs.blockIds.descript: Optional: only check references to these UUIDs. ID format/position problems are always checked for the whole file.
